lines.text: Project One: The Fire Station
Book 1
A Fire Station Begins
This Book Belongs To:
Mrs. Harper stood beside a picture of a bright new fire
station.
“Our town is building something special,” she said.
Leo nearly jumped from his seat.
“A fire station!”
Steph studied the picture.
“I like those big red doors.”
Maya noticed the drawings underneath it.
Ben raised his hand.
“Who plans a project that big?”
Vinny had another question.
“Do we get hard hats?”
Mrs. Harper smiled.
“You’re going to find out.”
The next morning, Mrs. Harper brought the Little Specs to the
construction site.
They saw dirt.
They saw gravel.
They saw wooden stakes.
They saw orange fencing.
And Leo saw a giant excavator.
But there was one thing they did not see.
“A fire station,” Leo said. “Where is it?”
Steph held up the picture from class.
“This is definitely the right place.”
Ben studied the site.
“Maybe the building has already started,” he said.
“We just can’t see it yet.”
A woman in a white hard hat walked toward them.
“I’m Ms. Rivera, the Project Manager,” she said. “My job is to
help keep the whole project organized.”
Ben’s eyes went straight to the plans under her arm.
A man with gray hair and a radio stepped beside her.
“And I’m Mr. Jackson, the Superintendent. I help organize what
happens out here every day.”
Leo stared at the excavator.
“So you know what all the machines are doing?”
Mr. Jackson grinned.
“I’d better.”
Before anyone went farther, Mr. Brooks gathered the group
beside the visitor entrance. “Every project starts with safety,”
he said. He showed them the rules. Hard hats. High-visibility
vests. Proper shoes. Stay with the group. Stay behind
barricades. Watch for moving equipment. “Construction sites
can be exciting,” Mr. Brooks said, “but we never let excitement
make us forget safety.”
Leo was still watching the excavator. He started forward
before fastening his vest. “Leo,” Vinny said. Leo stopped. Vinny
pointed to the open vest. “Oh.” Leo fastened it. Vinny nodded.
“Machines come after PPE.” Mr. Brooks smiled. “Good catch.”
Ms. Rivera reached into a small box. “There’s one more thing
we give people when they join a project.” She held up a small
round sticker. It showed the future fire station. Around the
edge it read: MIDDLE CREEK FIRE & RESCUE. And across the
bottom: STATION NO. 2. Leo’s eyes widened. “For our hard
hats?” “For your hard hats,” Ms. Rivera said.
“This sticker represents the project you’re going to follow from
the ground up.” One by one, the kids placed their stickers
wherever they wanted. Ben carefully lined his up. Maya
checked hers twice before pressing it down. Steph picked the
spot that looked best. Leo stuck his on quickly and grinned.
Vinny made sure his did not cover anything important. Mr.
Brooks nodded. “Now remember where you put them. Project
stickers stay with you.” The kids looked at one another’s hard
hats. Their first project had officially begun.
Nearby, a surveyor showed the kids small wooden stakes and
bright marks painted on the ground. “These tell us exactly
where the building belongs,” she explained. Maya looked
surprised. “A whole building from little sticks?” “And very
careful measurements,” said the surveyor.
She showed Maya how the distances on the site matched the
numbers on the plan. Maya checked one measurement. Then
another. Her eyes narrowed. She liked things to be exact.
Steph held the fire station drawing in front of her. She looked
at the empty dirt lot. Then back at the drawing. “There will be
three big truck doors over there,” she said. She pointed. “And
the entrance will be here.”
For a moment, Steph could almost see it. Walls. Windows. Fire
trucks. Firefighters hurrying in and out. Leo squinted. “I still see
dirt.” Steph smiled. “You have to imagine it first.”
Maya looked at one of the layout points again. Then she
checked the plan. Then the measurement. Then the plan again.
“That’s strange.” Ben walked over. “What is?” “This point
should be farther away.”
Ben checked the drawing. Steph looked toward the future
fire-truck driveway. “If the building moved that way,” she said,
“wouldn’t the driveway get smaller?” Maya nodded. Ben looked
toward Ms. Rivera. “We should ask.”
Ben approached Ms. Rivera. “Maya found something we don’t
understand.” Ms. Rivera did not laugh. She did not guess. She
said, “Show me.” The surveyor checked the measurements. Mr.
Jackson inspected the stake.
Then he noticed tire tracks nearby. “Aha.” The stake had been
bumped and was leaning away from its correct location. The
surveyor reset the point and checked again. “Now it matches.”
Ms. Rivera smiled. “Good question, team.”
Dr. Patel joined them. “What would happen if nobody checked
it?” Maya asked. Dr. Patel pointed toward the ground. “If the
foundation started in the wrong place, everything above it
could be affected.” “The walls?” asked Steph. “Yes.”
“The driveway?” asked Ben. “That too.” Leo looked at the
excavator. “So even that giant machine could dig in the wrong
place?” Dr. Patel nodded. Maya smiled. “Measure twice. Build
once.”
Once the layout was checked, the excavator began to work.
Leo could hardly stand still. The bucket dug into the soil.
Scoop. Lift. Swing. Dump. Mr. Jackson pointed toward the
marks on the ground.
“The operator isn’t just digging anywhere. The crew follows the
layout and the correct depth.” Leo watched carefully. “So the
machine is huge...” Mr. Jackson nodded. “...but the
measurements still have to be exact.” Leo grinned. “That
makes it even cooler.”
Soon, the kids saw pipes and conduits being placed below the
future floor. Leo tilted his head. “Why put those down there
now?” Ms. Rivera pointed toward the area where concrete
would eventually go. “Because once we cover everything with
concrete, getting underneath it becomes much harder.”
Ben looked at the schedule in her hands. “So one job has to
happen before another job can start.” “Exactly,” she said. Ben
smiled. Now that made sense.
Next came the reinforcing steel. Maya studied the steel bars
inside the forms. Dr. Patel explained, “Concrete is very strong,
and the steel helps it handle other forces too.” Workers
carefully checked the forms. They checked the steel. They
checked the measurements. Vinny noticed.
“They’re checking everything again?” Mr. Brooks nodded.
“Once concrete covers it, we want to know the work
underneath is right.” Vinny approved. “Checking twice sounds
pretty safe to me.”
Then came the day Leo had been waiting for. A concrete truck
rumbled onto the site. “YES!” Leo whispered. The Little Specs
watched from behind the barricade, their Fire Station stickers
now part of their hard hats. Concrete filled the forms. Workers
guided it into place. They smoothed it. They checked it.
Slowly, the foundation began to appear. Steph looked at her
drawing. Then at the concrete. “I can see it now,” she said. Ben
smiled. “It was there all along.” “We just needed the plan.”
Little Specs Construction Facts
What is a foundation?
A foundation supports a building and helps transfer its weight
safely into the ground.
What does a surveyor do?
Surveyors use special tools and careful measurements to
determine exactly where things should be built.
What is rebar?
Rebar is reinforcing steel placed inside concrete to help make
it stronger.
Why do pipes sometimes go under the floor?
Some pipes and conduits must be installed before concrete
covers the area.
Why do construction workers put stickers on hard hats?
Project stickers can represent jobs, companies, training,
milestones, or places a worker has been.
The Little Specs received their Fire Station project sticker
during safety orientation, just like project stickers are often
handed out at real jobsites.
Vinny’s Safety Corner
Construction sites can be dangerous.
Never enter an active construction site unless you are with an
authorized adult and following the site’s safety rules.
Next Time...
The foundation was ready. A truck rolled toward the site
carrying something very large. Leo stared. Maya looked at the
drawings. Steph looked up. Vinny checked the barricade. Ben
opened the schedule. Their Fire Station stickers were still on
their hard hats, exactly where each kid had placed them. The
fire station was finally ready to go...
